picks.showTitle: Dharma Seed: dharma talks and meditation instruction
picks.title: Donald Rothberg: Dukkha and the End of Dukkha: The Core Teaching of the Buddha
picks.summary: (Insight Meditation Community of Berkeley) The Buddha famously said, "I teach dukkha [suffering or reactivity or a sense of unsatisfactoriness] and the cessation of dukkha.” We explore this core teaching as it is expressed in the Four Noble Truths and the teachings of the Two Arrows and Dependent Origination, including ways that it can be confusing. We suggest ways to understand and implement this teaching both in formal meditation and in everyday life. (See document 328 below, on "Four Meanings of Dukkha, and Contact to Grasping in the Dependent Origination Model.")
picks.reason: In-depth exploration of dukkha and its cessation, core Buddhist teaching.

picks.showTitle: Zen Stories & Buddhist Teachings for Sleep by Midnight Monk
picks.title: Everything Changes - Sleep to Gentle Buddhist Teachings & Zen Stories for Peace and Rest
picks.summary: Tonight we will learn about the storms that pass through the mind. The moods that arrive without warning, stay longer than we would like, and leave as suddenly as they came.This episode draws on the Buddhist and Zen traditions to explore the five kinds of difficult weather that visit every mind, wanting, frustration, heaviness, restlessness, and doubt, and the ancient teaching that none of them are who we are. Through stories from across the Buddhist world and beyond, we discover what happens when we stop fighting our inner weather and learn to let it pass.This is a long, unhurried journey mea
picks.reason: Buddhist and Zen stories on impermanence and difficult mental states.

picks.showTitle: Angel City Zen Center - Beginners Only Podcast
picks.title: What to Love in Everything (Listening Practice) w/ Dave Cuomo
picks.summary: Dave brings us a brass tacks talk on meditation technique with a deep look at listening practice, inner listening, and intentional meditation practice in general. Can we engage in such things without spoiling the freewheeling just sitting shikantaza Zen is famous for? Can we scale the heights of the deepest meditative attainments with nothing but effortless ease? Is the peace we seek waiting quietly for us in the omnipresent roar of the A/C? Find out here!
picks.reason: A detailed talk on Zen meditation and listening practice with questions on effort and ease.

picks.showTitle: Angel City Zen Center - Beginners Only Podcast
picks.title: Tune In (Deep Listening) w/ Matthew Sherling
picks.summary: Resident poet Matthew is back with a deep exploration of the Buddhist and personal lore around listening practice, as wayward monks almost get sexy, a patron saint of listening saves us all by finding the sound of her own heart beat, Matthew reveals his awkward youthful misdeeds, and we dissolve the boundaries between ourselves and everybody else to find ourselves just a little more free. Are wisdom and compassion just another word for listening? Can we still function in the world if we drop the narrative of its story? Is listening to ourselves checking out the most fool proof way to tune in??
picks.reason: Explores Buddhist listening practice and compassion through personal stories.

picks.title: Standing in the World
picks.summary: Jody Hojin Kimmel, Sensei – ZCNYC – 8/29/26 – The Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta is where Buddha gives the four postures: walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. picks.reason: A talk on the Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta focusing on mindfulness of body postures.
